title: Forms and Events
subtitle: Build interactive forms and handle user events in React.
description: Learn event handlers, controlled inputs, form submission, validation basics and how React manages form data.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 6: Forms and Events. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Forms and Events”. The goal is to build interactive forms and handle user events in React.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
Controlled form fields keep their displayed value in React state, which makes validation and conditional feedback predictable. Each field should have a label and a clear value representation.

blocks.title: Sample 1: Forms and Events in practice

blocks.text: What to notice: focus on the part of the sample that demonstrates Build interactive forms and handle user events in React. Identify the input, the operation, and the result before making changes.

blocks.question: A controlled input displays stale text because the value is set but onChange never updates state. What is required?
options: Remove the value property.
Only change the border color.
Add another form element.
Update state in the change handler.
blocks.explanation: Controlled fields get their displayed value from state, so change handlers must update that state.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Controlled fields get their displayed value from state, so change handlers must update that state.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Controlled fields get their displayed value from state, so change handlers must update that state.

blocks.question: A form should show an error for an invalid email. What should the interface provide?
options: A clear message tied to the field and a way to correct it.
Only a silent failure.
A new browser tab without context.
A message that disappears before it can be read.
blocks.explanation: Helpful validation messages should identify the problem and support correction.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Helpful validation messages should identify the problem and support correction.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Helpful validation messages should identify the problem and support correction.

blocks.text: Handle submission explicitly, prevent the default browser action when appropriate, and validate before acting on the data. Client-side validation improves the experience but must not replace server-side checks for sensitive operations.

blocks.question: An app prevents browser form submission but never processes or validates the values. What is missing?
options: A more colorful submit button.
An explicit submit workflow that validates and handles the data.
A larger heading.
Another label pointing at the same input.
blocks.explanation: Preventing default behavior does not itself process or validate the form.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Preventing default behavior does not itself process or validate the form.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Preventing default behavior does not itself process or validate the form.

blocks.question: A reward begins at exactly 100 points, but the code awards it only when score is greater than 100. Which test exposes the bug?
options: Test only a score of 200.
Test a text value such as “high”.
Do not test the condition.
blocks.explanation: Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.

blocks.question: Two validation rules must both pass before submission. Which logical structure is appropriate?
options: Use OR if either rule must pass.
Skip validation once the page looks correct.
Combine both checks with the appropriate AND condition.
Run the same check forever.
blocks.explanation: AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
